intro.header: Representing Inequalities on a Number Line
intro.note: Answer each question in your workbook. Draw each number line carefully.
commonMistakes: Filled circle for < or > (should be open).
Open circle for ≤ or ≥ (should be filled).
−2 ≤ x is the same as x ≥ −2.
workedExample: ≥ includes −2, so a filled circle; arrow points right.
Read-back: filled ● at −2, arrow right = x ≥ −2 ✓
intro.visualAid: Open circle ○ means the boundary value is NOT included (< or >). Filled circle ● means it IS included (≤ or ≥). The arrow points towards all the numbers that make the inequality true.

questions.content: Show on a number line: a) x > 1  b) x ≤ 4
Show on a number line: a) x ≥ −3  b) x < 0
Write the inequality: a) open circle at 2, arrow right  b) filled circle at −1, arrow left
Show on a number line: a) x ≥ 5  b) x < −4  c) −2 ≤ x
Solve, then show on a number line: a) 2x + 1 > 7  b) 3x − 2 ≤ 10  c) 5 − 2x ≥ 1
Write and show: a) the number n is at least −1  b) the temperature t (°C) is below 5
Filled circle at −3, open circle at 4, shaded between. a) Write the inequality. b) List the integers.
Machine safe when t ≥ 10 and t < 35. a) Show each on a number line. b) Combine into one inequality. c) Is 35 °C safe? Explain.
